newsitem.title: JAPAN: Higher stocks to curb Japan kerosene import - trader.
newsitem.headline: Higher stocks to curb Japan kerosene import - trader.

text.p: Japan's kerosene imports towards winter are likely to be lower than earlier expected due to a recovery in kerosene inventories, traders said on Friday.
"With August kerosene stocks on par with last year's levels, it's just not realistic to expect a big jump in kerosene imports," one middle distillate trader said.

Kerosene stocks at the end of August grew 36.9 percent from a month earlier to 4.18 million kilolitres (kl) due to an increase both in domestic production and in imports, according to data released by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.

Because of unusually cold weather last winter and refiners' strategy to maintain low inventories to bolster the domestic market, stock levels in the spring were about 20 to 30 percent lower than a year earlier, prompting expectations of a substantial rise in imports towards this winter.

Although a sharp increase is unlikely, imports should gradually pick up towards the end of the year as Japan's kerosene production capacity is not large enough to meet all of the demand in the winter, traders said.
